source.title: From Text to Space: Mapping Abstract Spatial Models in LLMs during a Grid-World Navigation Task

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study probes individual units and ablates groups of them in a spatial-navigation task. Its results suggest that some units correlate with spatial features without being necessary for task performance, and the authors caution that units may be polysemantic. It does not test the stated neuron-job audit or attribution-graph claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports probes of LLaMA-3.1-8B activations and ablations, including evidence that some spatial-feature correlations generalize across prompt representations and that core-unit ablation has little effect on task success. These results bear on neuron-level analysis but do not count neuron poles by number of jobs, test explanations on held-out activating examples, or score explanations by predicting activations on new text. The grid-configuration R² plots and per-SIR counts are described qualitatively in the text, without extractable numeric values; cited results from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study probes LLaMA-3.1-8B units for linear correlations with spatial features and ablates unit groups in a grid-navigation task. It never audits neurons for how many jobs they have, never writes or scores neuron explanations, builds no attribution graphs, and studies no vision models. It only remarks that units may be polysemantic, citing monosemanticity work. No version is tested, so no verdicts are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, but the record omits the behavioural result. The authors conclude that Cartesian spatial representations give the best navigation performance, and that performance scales with model size across LLaMA-3 1B–90B. They also find that LLaMA-3.1-8B's internal grid representations are mostly format-dependent, with some format-invariant units for x/y position, border and action correctness. The action-correctness units also respond to unrelated spatial questions, yet are not necessary for the task. They caution these units may not be monosemantic and suggest the wider spatial system is distributed and likely polysemantic.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses linear probes for spatial features and ablates selected units in a grid-navigation task. It does not use the original neuron-pole job audit or evaluate written neuron explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: Representation format affects probing results: grid-state representations are mostly SIR-specific, with more generalization within an SIR class. Action-correctness unit counts differ by SIR; the JSON variant has the highest count. Ablation results reported here use JSON SIR.

fits_no_version.finding: Hundreds of units correlate with agent x position (448), y position (258), border status (373) and action correctness (286) across all six prompt formats. Shuffled controls give far fewer, e.g. 12 for action correctness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In LLaMA-3.1-8B, some individual units carry spatial-feature correlations that generalize across text formats of the same information.

fits_no_version.finding: The 286 core action-correctness units are more active on unrelated spatial questions (p=0.005), while random matched units are not (p=0.31). Core agent-position units show no such bias (p=0.78).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Format-invariant action-correctness units in LLaMA-3.1-8B also respond preferentially to spatial content outside the task.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating core action-correctness units (59%→55%) or position units (62%) barely changes success. Ablating all JSON-correlated units (59.7% of units) breaks output coherence. From this the authors infer, without measuring it, that the distributed spatial system is likely mostly polysemantic neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Format-invariant spatially correlated units are not necessary for simple grid navigation in LLaMA-3.1-8B. Their polysemanticity is asserted, not measured.

fits_no_version.finding: No unit correlates with the same specific grid cell across all six formats, though many do within single formats.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Place-cell-like unit selectivity in LLaMA-3.1-8B does not generalize across prompt formats.

record.problems: The mechanistic analysis covers only LLaMA-3.1-8B and a simple 5×5 navigation task. The study reports correlations and ablations rather than direct tests of whether neuron explanations predict activation on held-out examples. Some probes are based on input activations and may reflect prompt form; the authors explicitly note that many correlated units may reflect textual input and that units may be polysemantic. Ablating the full JSON-correlated group disrupted output coherence, limiting interpretation of its task effect.
record.rows_left_out: Qualitative grid-configuration R² and cross-SIR results are not separate rows because the text does not give the plotted numeric values. Per-SIR counts of correlated units are also not reported as numeric values in the text. Figure-only values were not extracted.

untested.parts: No audit of neuron poles by number of jobs. No Qwen3-32B. No share of single-job, two-job or not-yet-understood neurons.
No neuron-job shares in any model. Only LLaMA-3.1-8B is probed, with no MoE models and no scale comparison of interpretability.
No InceptionV1 or vision neurons. No analysis of the cat/car neuron, pose, or recursive generalization.
No manipulation of architecture, regularization or tool quality. No estimates of the share of interpretable neurons.
No attribution graphs, replacement models, or reconstruction-error comparison. Ablations test only task necessity of correlated units.
No explanations derived from activating examples, and no test of whether they predict firing.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The record's own versions guesses already mark all versions not_tested, which conflicts with its relation 'tests'/T5. Corrected to discusses/T6: the study's only contact with the claim is passing remarks on polysemanticity, inferred from ablation rather than measured. The 'units' here are hidden-state dimensions per layer (4096 per layer), which the paper calls parameters. They are probed by single-feature correlation, not by any account of what job each neuron does.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit neuron poles for one or two jobs or report a share of understood or not-yet-understood poles; uses LLaMA-3.1-8B rather than Qwen3-32B.
Does not compare neuron-job shares across models, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, or scale to trillions of parameters.
Does not analyze the InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not test the effects of architecture, regularization, or tool quality on neuron interpretability, or estimate interpretable-neuron shares for vision models.
Does not build attribution graphs or assess behavioral reconstruction error or replacement models. Its unit ablations do not directly test the version's attribution-graph claim.
Does not evaluate explanations written from activating examples against where a neuron fires.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.note: The paper reports that these units were predominantly in intermediate and deeper layers. This is a feature-correlation result, not a count of units with one interpretable job.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Silenced the 286 units correlated with action correctness across all SIR types during GWSOT trials.
rows.note: The authors describe the impact as almost none.
rows.check: Success moved from 59% to 55%, which the authors call almost no impact. No test is reported, and the ablation runs were only 100 trials. Against the study's own baseline this is no effect beyond control, so absent, not partial.

small number; 10 listed in Appendix B.3

rows.value: The model was unable to output coherent actions
rows.note: The ablated units comprised 59.7% of the total parameter count across all layers. The paper also says restricting ablation to middle layers 12–22 still disrupted output coherence.
rows.check: The ablated set was 59.7% of units across all layers, and only 10 trials were run. Loss of coherent output here says little beyond that massive ablation breaks the model. Keep the row, but treat it as a capability-breaking ablation, not a specific test.
